title: The Client Who Kept Changing the Rules
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] As a freelance designer, I used to believe that saying yes to every request was simply good customer service, even when the requests kept multiplying.
Narrator: Last spring, I took on a client who seemed straightforward at first, although the project quietly grew larger with almost every email he sent.
Narrator: [carefully] We had agreed on a fixed price for a basic website, five pages, one round of revisions, delivered within three weeks.
Narrator: However, by the second week, he was asking for an online store, a blog section, and a completely different color scheme, all without adjusting the budget.
Narrator: [reflective] At first, I said nothing, because I worried that pushing back might damage the relationship or cost me future work.
Narrator: As a result, I found myself working evenings and weekends just to keep pace with requests that were never part of our original agreement.
Narrator: [honestly] Eventually, I realized that if I kept absorbing every extra task silently, he would never understand where the actual boundaries were.
Narrator: I wrote a clear change record listing the original scope, new requests, work already completed, and effects on price and schedule.

Narrator: [seriously] I proposed returning to the original scope or approving a revised fee and timeline in writing before additional work continued. I also followed the agreed invoicing and payment terms.
Narrator: I sent that message with my hand practically shaking, half expecting him to disappear and never pay me at all.
Narrator: [gently] Instead, he apologized and admitted he hadn't realized how much he had added along the way, despite thinking each request seemed small individually.
Narrator: We agreed on a revised price, and even though the project still took longer than planned, the tension between us mostly disappeared.
Narrator: [encouraging] What struck me afterward was how differently he treated me once I had defined clear limits, in spite of my fear that boundaries would offend him.
Narrator: I used to think professionalism meant endless flexibility, but I've learned it actually depends on communicating expectations honestly from the very beginning.
Narrator: [sincere] Now I define deliverables, revision limits, payment stages, ownership, acceptance, and a change process at the start, then confirm later changes promptly.

quiz.question: What was originally agreed for the website project?
options: An online store with ten pages
Five pages with one round of revisions, in three weeks
quiz.explanation: The narrator says they agreed on five pages, one round of revisions, delivered within three weeks.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator stay silent at first about the extra requests?
options: She worried pushing back might damage the relationship or cost future work
quiz.explanation: She admits she worried that pushing back might damage the relationship or cost her future work.

quiz.question: What two options did the narrator propose to the client?
options: Cancel the project or refund him
Finish for free or quit immediately
Reduce the project back to its original scope, or adjust the price fairly
quiz.explanation: She proposed reducing the scope back to the original agreement, or adjusting the price to reflect the extra work.

quiz.question: How did the client react to her message?
options: He apologized and admitted he hadn't realized how much he'd added
quiz.explanation: He apologized, admitting he hadn't realized how much he had added along the way.

quiz.question: What lesson does the narrator take from this experience?
options: Communicating expectations honestly from the beginning matters more than constant flexibility
quiz.explanation: She concludes that professionalism depends on communicating expectations honestly from the start, not endless flexibility.

quiz.question: Why did the project keep expanding?
options: The original agreement included a store
Small separate requests were never evaluated as a combined scope change
quiz.explanation: Individually small additions created a large unpriced workload.

quiz.question: What made the narrator’s first response weak?
options: Silence hid the cost and allowed expectations to remain unclear

quiz.question: What should a change record specify?
options: New deliverables, price, schedule, responsibilities, and approval
quiz.explanation: A proper change affects more than the task list.

quiz.question: Why is the client’s apology not the only protection needed?
options: A repeatable written process should not depend on goodwill
quiz.explanation: Professional safeguards must survive a less cooperative case.

quiz.question: What does the narrator now understand by professionalism?
options: Clear commitments, timely communication, and fair handling of changes
